content: 1. Levonorgestrel, ethinyl estradiol, and ferrous bisglycinate may interact with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors can increase plasma hormone concentrations. It is recommended to use a nonhormonal contraceptive in such cases. 2. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lidocaine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical monitoring is advised, especially when co-administered with antiarrhythmics. 3. Lonafarnib increases the levels or effects of tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Lonafarnib is a weak P-gp inhibitor, and minimal concentration changes in P-gp substrates may lead to serious toxicities. Dose reduction of P-gp substrates may be required. 4. Lopinavir increases elvitegravir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with lopinavir/ritonavir significantly increases elvitegravir levels. The recommended dose of elvitegravir is 85 mg orally once daily with lopinavir/ritonavir, except for 400/100 mg BID regimens. 5. Lorlatinib decreases elvitegravir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 6. Cobicistat increases losartan levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 7. Cobicistat increases lumacaftor/ivacaftor levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Due to lumacaftor's induction effect on CYP3A, the net exposure of ivacaftor at steady state is not expected to exceed monotherapy levels. No dose adjustment is needed when CYP3A inhibitors are initiated in patients on lumacaftor/ivacaftor. However, when starting lumacaftor/ivacaftor in patients on strong CYP3A inhibitors, reduce the dose to one tablet daily for the first week, then resume the recommended dose. 8. Cobicistat increases lumateperone levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary, with a recommended dose of 5 mg/day when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 9. Magnesium oxide decreases elvitegravir levels by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Separate doses by at least 2 hours to avoid reduced plasma concentrations. 10. Cobicistat increases maraviroc levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce maraviroc dose to 150 mg BID when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 11. Momelotinib increases tenofovir alafenamide toxicity by plasma protein binding competition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Momelotinib, a BCRP inhibitor, may increase the exposure of BCRP substrates, necessitating dose adjustments. 12. Cobicistat increases methylprednisolone levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 13. Nefazodone increases elvitegravir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Elvitegravir is a CYP3A4 substrate, and co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase its levels. 14. Cobicistat increases metoprolol levels or effects by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 15. Cobicistat increases mexiletine levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical monitoring is advised, especially when co-administered with antiarrhythmics. 16. Cobicistat increases mifepristone levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration is necessary, adjust mifepristone dose based on the patient's current regimen. 17. Cobicistat increases mirtazapine levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 18. Cobicistat increases mirvetuximab soravtansine levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase exposure to unconjugated DM4, the cytotoxic component of the antibody-drug conjugate, raising the risk of adverse reactions. 19. Cobicistat increases mometasone (inhaled or intranasal) levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This increases the risk of systemic corticosteroid side effects. Caution and monitoring are advised. 20. Cobicistat increases naldemedine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor for potential adverse effects if co-administered with P-gp inhibitors. 21. Cobicistat increases nefazodone levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Nefazodone also increases cobicistat levels. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 22. Nelfinavir increases elvitegravir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Elvitegravir is a CYP3A4 substrate, and co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase its levels. 23. Cobicistat increases netupitant/palonosetron levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Netupitant is mainly metabolized by CYP3A4, but no dosage adjustment is required. 24. Nicardipine increases elvitegravir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Elvitegravir is a CYP3A4 substrate, and co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase its levels. 25. Cobicistat increases nifedipine levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 26. Cobicistat increases nilotinib levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dosage adjustment of nilotinib may be necessary when co-administered with cobicistat. Refer to nilotinib prescribing information for dosing instructions. 27. Cobicistat increases nintedanib levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. If adverse effects occur, management may require dose reduction, interruption, or discontinuation of therapy. 28. Nirmatrelvir increases tenofovir alafenamide levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration may increase systemic exposures of tenofovir. 29. Cobicistat increases norgestrel levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic concentrations of norgestrel, raising the risk of adverse effects. 30. Cobicistat increases nortriptyline levels or effects. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to achieve the desired effect, using the lowest feasible dose, and monitor its response during co-administration with TCAs and cobicistat. 31. Cobicistat increases oliceridine levels or effects by affecting CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration is necessary, less frequent dosing may be required. Monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust subsequent doses accordingly. 32. Cobicistat increases omeprazole levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 33. Cobicistat increases ondansetron levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 34. Orlistat decreases elvitegravir levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Loss of virological control has been reported in HIV-infected patients taking orlistat concomitantly. Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently, and discontinue orlistat if increased viral load is confirmed. 35. Cobicistat increases osilodrostat levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the osilodrostat dose by half when co-administered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 36. Oteseconazole increases tenofovir alafenamide levels or effects. Oteseconazole, a BCRP inhibitor, may increase the effects and risk of toxicities of BCRP substrates. Use the lowest starting dose of BCRP substrates or consider dose reduction. 37. Cobicistat increases ospemifene levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 38. Cobicistat increases oxycodone levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors is necessary, monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust the dose until stable drug effects are achieved. 39. Cobicistat increases paclitaxel levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 40. Cobicistat increases panobinostat levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the panobinostat starting dose to 10 mg if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 41. Cobicistat increases paricalcitol levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 42. Cobicistat increases paroxetine levels or effects. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to achieve the desired effect, using the lowest feasible dose, and monitor its response during co-administration with SSRIs and cobicistat. 43. Cobicistat increases perphenazine levels or effects. A decrease in the dose of antipsychotics metabolized by CYP3A or CYP2D6 may be needed upon co-administration. 44. Cobicistat increases pitavastatin levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. For HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors not contraindicated with cobicistat, start with the lowest recommended dose and titrate while monitoring for safety. 45. Cobicistat increases polatuzumab vedotin levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase unconjugated MMAE exposure, raising the risk of toxicity.
